given: a stock record already exists for a given SKU and location pair
when: the team member files stock again for that same SKU and location pair
then: the existing record for that pair is updated in place so only one record exists for the pair, with no duplicate stored and no error surfaced

independence.rationale: AC1 and AC2 concern a first write and its read-back; this AC covers the distinct outcome of a repeat write on an existing (sku, location) pair collapsing to a single record, which can break (duplicate stored or error shown) independently of the first-write and retrieval behaviors.

architectural_notes: E2E write-collision path enforcing the (sku, location) uniqueness invariant (PI1). The service layer owns the collision-resolution business rule (upsert semantics) and wraps the read-then-write in a single transaction (PI4, transactions belong to the service, never the domain); the repository realizes the atomic upsert against the DB unique constraint so a repeat write updates in place rather than storing a duplicate or surfacing an error. The DB-level unique constraint is the ultimate guard, verified against the real branch, so this AC is the persistence contract's front line.
